description: One verdict, pass / warn / fail, for a file against a spec or your own limits, rule by rule: each rule has the measured value, its status (validated, proxy, beta), the limit, an outcome (pass, fail, uncertain, information, not-measured), how far past the limit and what to do. There is no composite score: the verdict follows from the rules. A proxy only informs; a value past its limit by less than the margin of its measure is uncertain and gives warn; a measure that could not be taken is not-measured. Critical faults (voice.clipping, chain.dropoutCount, level.peak) are on by default. Send spec or limits, not both. spec: starting-point, target-spotify, target-youtube, target-tidal, target-amazon-music, target-apple-music, target-podcast, target-tiktok, target-instagram, target-soundcloud, target-deezer, target-ebu-broadcast, target-atsc-broadcast. limits: an object per lens id, up to 30, each {min?, max?}, for example {"loudness.integrated": {"min": -17, "max": -15}}; lens ids: https://audiolab.tools/lenses (room lenses need a clap or sweep and are not taken here). Guide: https://audiolab.tools/docs/start/qc-in-one-call Audio source: a public https URL, or a local file path (`path`).

critical.description: Which critical faults are on. All three by default; [] switches them off.

limits.description: Your own limits per lens id: {"loudness.integrated": {"min": -17, "max": -15}}. Send spec or limits, not both.

path.description: Path to a LOCAL audio file on this machine. It is read here and uploaded to the AudioLab API for measuring, so you do not need to host it publicly (files up to 4 MB go in the request body; larger ones, up to 150 MB, upload over a signed URL and are swept from storage within the hour). Provide exactly one of url or path.

spec.description: A named set of limits: starting-point or target-<preset>. Send spec or limits, not both.

url.description: Public https URL to the audio file. Provide exactly one of url or path.

name: check_qc
title: QC verdict against a spec or your own limits
